newsitem.title: UK: Bishop resigns after running off with divorcee.
newsitem.headline: Bishop resigns after running off with divorcee.

text.p: A Scottish Roman Catholic bishop, reported by media to have run off with a divorced woman, told the Pope on Monday he was resigning from his post.

The Bishop of Argyll and the Isles, the Rt Rev Roderick Wright, 55, sparked a furore in church circles when he disappeared on September 9 at the same time as divorced mother Kathleen Macphee also went missing from her Highlands home.
In a statement to Pope John Paul, released by the Catholic Church in Scotland, Wright said he was "physically and spiritually" unable to sustain the responsibilities of his office.

"I ask your forgiveness and your prayers. I wish to remain a committed member of the Catholic Church. I now wish time and privacy to reflect on my future as I await acceptance of my resignation as bishop," he said.
Media reports say Wright counselled Macphee, a mother of three in her early 40s, after the breakup of her marriage.
The church said he emerged from hiding on Sunday to meet Cardinal Thomas Winning, Scotland's most senior Catholic clergyman, but a church official declined to say where the bishop was.

"Bishop Wright is also very anxious to ask forgiveness for all the harm and hurt caused by his actions, especially to the members of his own family and Kathleen Macphee's family and to all those who were supportive and good to him," the church said.
